ios.desc:
Kill two birds with one stone.

"Probably the best game in the world" - friend of developer

Launch the stone with the handy slingshot. You have five tries to knock both birds out of the sky. You can rebound one bird into another, or try to hit both with the stone.

No ads, no in-app purchases. Ideal for waiting rooms, bus stops, waiting for an elevator, or a 24 hour gaming marathon.

Features:
- Earn robots, which will automatically beat a level for you.
- Kill 3 birds with one stone? 4? How high can you go? (the answer is 5, because any more than that is unreasonable)
- Game always starts with sound disabled to allow for sneaky play all the time.

I built this for a bit more than just "making money" (wanted some experience), and it is still early days. But I made an iOS game:

quotes.story_title: Ask HN: What's a side project you built to make money that hasn't?

quotes.text:
I wrote nearly all of https://apps.apple.com/us/app/two-birds-one-stone/id1539646329 on a train without internet. It was about a half hour journey, and I found that in such a short amount of time, I would set a small goal and work in a very distraction free way to achieve it. It was very good for doing small things, but sometimes doing larger things (like big refactors) is a bit more difficult. On occasion, I would also dedicate a train ride to just writing up a todo list.

I gave myself the rule of no internet while on the train, so sometimes I would just accumulate a list of questions I wanted to answer later.

There is definitely something to it, and you can get heaps done, but it needs to be supported with some non-train time (e.g. for me, it was all the app store stuff, debugging with real hardware, etc)

I made this iOS game:

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/two-birds-one-stone/id1539646329

I have wanted to be able to play this game for a long time, and probably thanks to pandemic, I did the work to enable it to be shared with others. It has made a grand total of 3 sales this year, and that isn't really bothering me (the main frustration is the apple developer fee...)

There is various info (including a trailer of sorts) here:

https://ideationapps.com/
quotes.story_title: Ask HN: What is your “I don't care if this succeeds” project?
